correctness.rationale: The mixed triangle conditions give exactly the stated metric inequalities. In the scalar problem boundedness forces constant preservation, and simultaneous pair-permutation averaging reduces arbitrary extensions to the parameter θ. A zero-sum coefficient vector has sharp scalar oscillation norm half its ℓ¹ norm. Clipping to [−1/(n−1),1] decreases the maximum: below it the negative mass at the n−2 nondistinguished indices already exceeds the endpoint mismatch cost, and above it the positive mass at the mismatched source exceeds its value at 1. On that interval the matched cost decreases and the unmatched cost increases. Equalizing them, or clipping the intersection at the lower endpoint, gives the stated two formulas. The target–target cost is |θ|/s and is already controlled by s≥|a−b| on the intersection branch and s≥a−b≥b/(n−2) on the plateau. The identity on X enforces the floor 1. Nonnegative coefficients summing to one give the same upper bound for any real Banach target by transport at unit equilateral cost; norm-one scalarization along a unit vector of any nonzero target gives the unrestricted lower bound. The sample plateau is feasible and equals 40/39. The support statement is about the displayed optimal kernel, not a general uniqueness theorem, particularly on the norm-one region.
residual_risks: The numerical finite LPs are corroboration only and were not replayed. No classification of all optimal operators is inferred.

evidence: Choose the common raw c>0 solving (1−ca)_++(n−1)(1−cb)_+=1. The prior theorem certifies the lower bound max(1,c) already on X∪{y_i}. The coefficient at x_j in row i is (1−c d(y_i,x_j))_+. These rows have exactly the displayed coefficients by the two elementary cases ca≤1 and ca≥1.

Between rows i,k all other coefficients cancel, leaving the difference of (1−ca)_+ and (1−cb)_+ times f(x_i)−f(x_k). Its absolute scalar coefficient is at most c|a−b|≤cs by positive-part Lipschitzness and the triangle inequality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This proves the full joint upper bound, the exact s-independence and the same support-loss kernel using the prior proof formula with no new joint minimax. The estimate holds even when c<1 and the norm floor is active. Scalarization carries the matching row lower bound to every nonzero real Banach target.

originality.rationale: The earlier indexed equilateral one-point theorem gives the exact row cost and the positive-part coefficients before applying the floor 1. In this paired metric the rows differ only by swapping the matched and unmatched entries, so the positive-part formula and the triangle inequality immediately give all inter-target constraints. This is a direct corollary for every n, not merely an analogy to one-point extension. A distinct cyclic-triples record also explicitly covers the whole n=3 subfamily.

value.rationale: Simultaneous extension at sharp norm is naturally motivated, but in this slice the known positive-part row profile and automatic two-coordinate estimate leave no independent bottleneck. The nonunit support plateau for n≥4 was already present in the general row profile and survives matching by a one-line metric inequality. The submitted scope gives no new phenomenon beyond that corollary and no genuine distinct remainder to repair.
residual_risks: The result may be useful as an application of the row theorem; that does not make the submitted claim an independent scientific contribution.
